title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and polyneuropathy.

HPI
The patient is a 64-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his chronic conditions. He reports persistent tingling and "pins and needles" sensations in both feet, which he describes as a common symptom of his polyneuropathy. He states that the sensations are more pronounced at night. Regarding his type 2 diabetes, the patient reports that he is strictly following a healthy eating plan. He denies any episodes of extreme thirst or frequent urination since the last visit. He currently manages his glucose levels through diet and exercise alone.

Medication List
Multivitamins, Vitamin B12.

Exam
General: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
Extremities: Decreased sensation to light touch and vibration in bilateral toes. No active ulcers or skin breakdown noted on the feet.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Currently managed with a diet-controlled approach.
2. Polyneuropathy: Chronic symptoms of peripheral neuropathy persisting.

Plan
Continue current diet and exercise regimen for management of type 2 diabetes. Monitor sensation in lower extremities. Follow up in three months.
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: the combination code E11.42 captures both.

distractors.why: Coding the two separately misses the presumed link.
